questions.question: Taken as a whole, what broad musical style does this song most closely resemble? Which two sonic features support that judgment?
Does the lead vocal sound male or female? What are the lowest note, highest note, and total range of the main melody across the song?
In the opening phrase of the first chorus, is the melody shaped mainly by small oscillations between neighboring notes or by a succession of large leaps?
At the beginning of the first verse, does the voice enter immediately at the start of the bar, or after a one-beat rest? On which beat does it enter, and what effect does this create?
Which chords occur from beginning to end in the first verse? What are their scale degrees, inversions, extensions, and principal connections in the home key?
Around which tonic and mode is the song primarily organized? Which frequently recurring dominant-to-tonic progression best supports that conclusion?
Across the complete vocal melody, what are the lowest and highest notes? How wide is the range, and in which sections do the two extremes occur?
When the main melody of the first chorus ends, which chord does the final C7 resolve to? What is the relationship of that resolution in the home key?
A continuous dominant-function chain occurs at the end of the second pre-chorus. Name its three chords, give their scale degrees in the song's home key, and identify the target of each step.
From the start of the main melody in the first chorus through its return to the tonic Fm chord, what are all the notes and rhythms? Write the melody out bar by bar.
Judging from the harmony, instrumentation, and overall texture, what broad musical style does this song most closely resemble?
Compare the same melodic theme at the openings of the first and second choruses. Which pitches and rhythms remain unchanged, and how do the entrance and the third bar change?
Has the bridge returned to the tonic chord by its ending? What exact chord does it stop on, and why does the result still sound open?
In the first phrase of the bridge, count in four and identify where the vocal opening and the next principal notes enter. Why do these placements create a syncopated feel?
Which clear non-diatonic chords occur in the second verse? What are their scale-degree origins, target chords, and actual functions in E♭ major?
Across the full song, is the basic pulse grouped in three or in four?
What are the lowest and highest notes of the complete main melody? In which sections do they occur, and what is the total range?
Which three main classes of instrument accompany the voice in the first verse? Does the overall arrangement sound sparse or dense?
The first chorus contains the same non-diatonic dominant-seventh resolution twice. Identify the dominant-seventh chord and its target, and explain their scale degrees and resolution in B♭ major.
What is the complete chord progression of the second chorus? What are the scale degrees, inversions, and extensions of these chords, and in what harmonic state does the ending remain?
What broad musical style does this song most closely resemble? Which two features of its accompaniment or groove support your answer?
Across the song, what are the lead vocal's lowest and highest notes, and in which sections do they occur? In which register is most of the vocal melody concentrated?
In the first verse, does the lead vocalist begin the first phrase immediately on the bar's opening beat, or after leaving one beat empty? What is the opening pitch?

In the short progression immediately before the final return to the tonic in the outro, what is the full name of the dominant chord and which altered tone does it contain? Which chord does it actually resolve to, and how should both chords be labeled in the home key?
How does the harmony progress through the first verse? Which inversions, sevenths, and ninths occur, and on what function does the section end?
What is the song's principal key? Which recurring type of harmonic return most clearly confirms this center?
Considering only the lead-vocal melody and not the accompaniment, what are the lowest pitch, highest pitch, and complete range? In which sections do the two extremes occur approximately?
In the first verse, does the lead vocal enter as soon as the section begins, or does the accompaniment play for one bar first? When the voice does enter, on which beat does it begin?

In the latter half of the bridge, a three-chord progression changes from bright to dark before moving to another chord. Identify the three chords, and explain the origin and function of the middle chord.
What are all the lead-vocal pitches and rhythms in the first chorus, bar by bar, including bars of complete vocal rest?
After hearing the full song, which major key is its most stable center? Which recurring progression best supports that conclusion?
Compare the core melodies of the first and third choruses. Which elements clearly preserve the same framework, and which pitches or chords change? Do these changes alter the G-major center?
In the first four equal-length notes at the opening of the first chorus, does the melody keep ascending, or does it rise and then turn back? What are the four pitches?

A particularly sharp-sounding non-diatonic dominant-seventh chord occurs in the first half of the bridge. Identify the chord, its chromatic note, and its target, and explain whether it creates a true modulation.
What are the pitches and rhythms of the lead-vocal melody across the eight bars of the first verse? Which short motive recurs, and how are the main pauses created?
Judging from the accompaniment timbres, harmonic language, and vocal atmosphere, what broad style does this song most closely resemble? Which audible features support the classification?
Across the song, which of B♭ major and G minor is the global key, and which is only tonicized locally? Give one audible chord chain supporting each conclusion.
In the first phrase after the first chorus begins, is the melody dominated by large leaps or by oscillation around adjacent notes? Around which pitches does it repeatedly move?
In the bar where the first verse vocal actually begins, does the voice enter on a strong beat or on a weak subdivision? How long is the preceding rest, and how long does the first note last?
What is the complete chord progression of the first verse? What are the scale degree and function of each chord in B♭ major, and which chords are non-diatonic?
Judging from the song's groove, instrumentation, and harmonic color, what broad pop style does it most closely resemble, and why?

Across all vocal sections, what are the lowest and highest notes of the main melody? In what kind of section does the highest note mainly occur, and how does it compare with the melody's usual register?
At the beginning of the first verse, does the lead vocal enter immediately, or wait until beat 4 for its first group of notes?
Why does the harmony suddenly darken in the latter half of the bridge? Which chord causes the change, and what function does it serve in the current key?
Give the complete chord sequence and scale degrees of the first verse. How are its seventh chords, extensions, and brief tonicization organized?
After hearing the entire song, is F♯ perceived as a major or minor tonic? Which recurring resolution provides the strongest support?
Are the first and second choruses literal repetitions, or variations on the same chorus framework? What evidence comes from the opening melody and the harmony in the middle?
When the vocal line truly begins in the first verse, does its first note fall on beat 1 or on the second half of beat 1?
Why do the long F♯–E♯–F♯ notes at the end of the second verse both fit the harmony and retain forward tension? On what function do these bars finally stop?
List all the chords and scale degrees of the first chorus in order. Which seventh and ninth chords, and which shifts between minor and major, shape its path of tension?
What musical style best describes the song as a whole? Give one supporting feature from its core instrumentation and one from its harmonic language.
How do the three chorus endings differ in their treatment of dominant tension? What are the key chords, scale degrees, and outcomes of each?
Does the first chorus begin with an upbeat, or does the singer enter directly on beat 1 with a relatively long note?
How does the melody in the first bar of the first chorus outline the tonic chord? Which note lies outside the seventh chord's basic chord tones and adds extended color?
Give the bridge's complete chord progression and scale degrees. How does the oscillating color of its first half turn into a functional drive toward the dominant in the second half?
What is the song's home key? Identify one recurring dominant-to-tonic connection that most clearly confirms it, giving the exact chords and scale degrees.

Are the opening melodies of the first and second verses repeated literally, or is the rhythmic shape rewritten while retaining the same pitch center? What specifically differs between their first complete vocal bars?
Does the melody at the opening of the first chorus keep ascending, or does it oscillate between two adjacent notes? On which note does it finally land?
Before the final return to G♯m7 in the second verse, which bass note and inversion does the dominant-seventh chord use? How does that bass move into the tonic chord?
Reconstruct the nine-bar main melody of the first chorus bar by bar. What are all its pitches, rhythms, rests, and ties across barlines?
What broad genre does this song most closely resemble? Which features of its harmony, instrumentation, or groove support that judgment?
Across the full song, is the lead vocalist male or female? What are the vocal melody's lowest pitch, highest pitch, and overall range?
In the final two bars of the first chorus, which chord moves to which chord? What are their scale degrees in the home key, and does this ending reach closure?

In the second verse, a non-diatonic dominant-seventh chord follows A♯m7. Identify that chord and its target, give the scale degrees of the progression in the home key, and explain whether it constitutes a true modulation.
Reconstruct the complete main melody of the first chorus bar by bar. What are all its pitches, rhythms, rests, and ties across barlines?
Does the song maintain a basic pulse in four or in three?
Do all three choruses return to the tonic chord before their respective sections end? What is the final harmonic destination of each chorus?
At the start of the first chorus, does the lead vocal enter directly on the opening beat, or leave an eighth note empty and enter on a weak position?

The first pre-chorus contains a three-chord non-diatonic ii–V-type progression. Identify the full progression, give each chord's scale degree relative to the global key, and determine whether a genuine modulation occurs.
What is the complete harmonic framework of the first verse? For each bar, identify the chord's scale degree, inversion, extension, and any suspension.
Which pitch and tonic chord sound most like “home” across the song, and is the key major or minor?
Does the lead vocal sound male or female? What are the lowest note, highest note, and total range of the lead-vocal melody?

Listen to the end of the first chorus and the beginning of the next section. Does the chorus resolve to the tonic within its own section, or postpone the resolution? Give the exact chords and scale degrees of the cross-sectional progression.
A non-diatonic dominant-seventh chord appears in the second chorus. Identify it and the chord that follows, and explain the progression's scale degrees and function in the original key.
Which non-diatonic chords occur in the first verse? Give each chord's name, scale degree, location, and target chord.
What musical style does this song most closely resemble? Give the two most persuasive audible features supporting your answer.

Are the three choruses literal repetitions of the same core vocal passage, or do they retain its framework while changing it progressively? What specifically remains the same and changes in their opening two bars?
When does the lead vocal enter after the first chorus begins? How much empty space precedes it, and on which beat does its first note fall?

In the first pre-chorus, the harmony suddenly darkens in a brief progression. What are the exact chords before and after the change? Explain their scale degrees, origin, and function in the global key, and determine whether a modulation occurs.
How does the first verse move among tonic, subdominant, and dominant functions from beginning to end? Give the exact chord, scale degree, inversion, and extension in every bar.
Which chord repeatedly serves as the song's point of arrival? Identify the home key and support your answer with a recurring progression and the sound of the cadences.
Compare the three choruses in sequence. How do their harmonic openings, orchestral layers, and degree of closure differ, and what structural role does each chorus play?
In the introduction, which foreground and sustained timbres first establish the sense of space? What role does the rhythm section play there?
At the opening of the second chorus, a conspicuous chromatic pitch appears in the bass. What is that bass pitch and chord? Explain its inversion, function, and actual destination.

Give the chordal framework and scale degrees of the main vocal portion of the third chorus. Distinguish the chords that produce genuine dominant resolutions from the chord used only for chromatic color.
Which chord provides the strongest sense of final arrival in the song? What key does it establish, and which turnaround proves it most clearly?
Where do the lowest and highest notes of the lead-vocal melody occur? What is the total range, and how does it reflect the lift in the latter part of the song?
On which beat does the lead vocal enter in the first phrase of the first verse? What are the opening rest and first note values?
In the first two bars of the first chorus, where are the rests inserted? Give the principal pitches and values in each bar, and compare their attack density.
Give the complete chord framework and scale degrees of the first verse. For each of its two dominant-function chords, identify the actual successor and the section's final destination.
Bright and dark relative-key colors alternate repeatedly through the song. Which chord is the true final center? Support your answer with returns at section boundaries and cadential progressions.

The three choruses use similar material, but which one functions as a shortened transition, and which inserts an instrumental gap in the middle and achieves the fullest closure? Describe the structural differences you hear.
In the introduction, which three basic instruments carry the low frequencies, beat, and harmonic texture respectively?
At the beginning of the second verse, how do the entrance and the following bars change in attack density and melodic direction? Give the key pitches and locations of rests.
Summarize the complete harmonic path of the bridge and identify the two most strongly goal-directed chords, one in the middle and one at the end. What is each chord, and where does it actually lead?
What broad pop style does this song most closely resemble? Explain your answer through the guitar accompaniment, drum groove, and harmonic color.
How does the song move from its opening into the first theme, and how do later sections add and remove timbres to create a thin-to-thick-to-reduced trajectory?
How does the lead vocalist use sustained notes, rests, and ties across barlines to shape breathing in the first verse? Summarize the most prominent rhythmic feature.
In the final four bars of the first chorus, which melodic pitches are tied across successive barlines? What contour do they form, and how much silence follows the last tied note?
Give the complete chord framework and scale degrees of the first chorus. Where do its two most directional tension chords actually lead?
Which stable center does the music repeatedly return to? Identify the home key and support it through dominant-to-tonic connections and section endings.
How does this relatively long song avoid a mechanical verse–chorus cycle? Explain through its mid-song turn, the bridge's function, and the orchestration of the final chorus.
Which timbres carry the main buildup in the introduction, and why does this section feel more suspended than the verse?
In the first phrase of the second chorus, on which metrical position does the lead vocal enter? How do the sustained note across beats and the tie at the end of the phrase create forward motion?
Give the chord framework of the third chorus and explain how its three most prominent tension points actually lead to the chords that follow.
What broad pop style does this song most closely resemble? Which timbres and dynamic changes support your classification?
Both dark and bright relative-key regions are prominent. What is the ultimate tonal center? Support your answer with the core cycle, the dominant chord's actual resolutions, and its leading tone.
Which timbres form the foreground and sustained background layers in the introduction? How do they create depth at the opening?
How does the short vocal phrase at the end of the introduction cross the low and high registers and tie into the first verse? Give its pitch skeleton and explain the cross-sectional tie.
Give the principal pitches and durations in the first four bars of the first chorus. How do the two ties across barlines shape the phrase's momentum?
Which points of arrival reveal the song's home key? Name the most stable chord and support it with a recurring progression.
Compare the lead-vocal registers in the first two choruses. What is the highest note of each, which chorus reaches higher, and how is the high-register material rewritten?
In the first bar where the first verse actually begins to sing, at what position within the beat does the lead vocal enter? Which note values predominate afterward?

Which chord at the end of the first verse has the strongest directional pull? Where does it actually resolve across the section boundary, and how should its scale degree and function be labeled in the home key?

In the three bars near the end of the first chorus, how does the lead vocal reach the section's highest note and descend again? Reconstruct the key note sequence and ties, and explain what chord tone the longest high note is before and after the harmony changes.
Which chord should ultimately be heard as the tonic? Identify the key and support it with recurring arrivals and one secondary-dominant resolution.
What are the lead vocal's lowest and highest notes, and in which sections do they occur? What is the total range, and how is its upper limit reached later in the song?
In the introduction, which keyboard instrument and which two kinds of sustained timbre create the orchestral opening?
Compare the first two sung bars of the first verse. How do they differ in attack density, rests, and the use of a tie across the barline?
Give the bridge's chord framework and scale degrees. How do its key chromatic chords connect the surrounding harmony, and where do they actually lead?
How many beats make up the recurring metric group across the song? How does that grouping affect the melody's rocking motion?
Large portions of the song remain around the minor dominant and relative-major region. How can the true tonal center be identified without being misled by these prolonged areas?
Across the first four bars of the first verse, does the melody expand upward overall, or descend gradually from a stable pitch? Identify its principal points of arrival.
A conspicuously prolonged note occurs in the middle of the first chorus. What pitch is it, how many barlines does it cross, where does it end, and how are the rests arranged afterward?
Give the principal pitch sequence and rhythmic organization of each of the first four bars of the first chorus, then summarize the melodic contour.
Which chord ultimately sounds like home? Identify the key and support it with key progressions from the opening and later cadences.
In what kinds of section do the lead vocal's lowest and highest notes occur? What is the full range, and how does the later high point differ from the verse's usual register?
Does the lead vocal sing continuously through the first bar of the second chorus? Where does the brief rest occur, and what note values surround it?
After the melody descends twice toward the song's lowest note in the first half of the first verse, how does it rise again? Identify the lowest note and the most conspicuous leap.
Give the chord framework and scale degrees of the improvisatory section. Where do its stepwise opening bass and its chromatic midsection tension actually lead?
What broad pop style does this song most closely resemble? Which guitar, rhythm-section, and keyboard timbres support that judgment?
Compare the phrase length, use of repetition, and instrumental focus of the three choruses. What structural role does each one play?
At the beginning of the bridge, how does the first emphasized pitch of each of the first three bars rise step by step?
Why does the vocal rhythm in the first bar of the first chorus sound interrupted? Give the basic sequence of notes and rests.
Summarize the harmonic framework and scale degrees of the first verse. How does the suddenly darker chord at its end hand the music into the chorus?
Which tonic chord does the song ultimately return to? Identify the key and name the dominant-to-tonic connection with a raised leading tone that confirms it most strongly.

Does the song build gradually before presenting its core theme, or begin with the theme immediately? How do the first, second, and final thematic sections divide the work through instrumentation and length?
At the beginning of the first verse, around which pitch does the lead vocal initially linger, and how does it then rise stepwise to the phrase's high point?
How do two adjacent bars in the latter half of the first verse contrast in attack density? Give the long-and-short pattern of the first bar and the notes and rests of the second.
Give the principal pitches and rhythm of the first four bars of the bridge. How do the two ties across barlines connect short phrases with long rests?
What modern pop style does this song most closely resemble? Which aspects of its rhythm section, low end, and later instrumental layers support your answer?
Where do the lead vocal's lowest and highest notes occur? What is the complete range, and how does the melody approach and leave the highest note?
What repeated note values make up the short phrase in the first bar of the first chorus, and how much empty space remains at the end?
Around which pitches does the final phrase of the first verse revolve? Reconstruct the repeated motion in the first half and the pitch organization of the ending.
Give the bridge's chord framework and scale degrees. What inversion is the slash chord, where does it actually lead, and how does it prolong the section?
Does the song gradually build through a verse before introducing its core theme, or present the theme immediately? How does the later large-scale form return to it?

Across the song, are the three choruses closest to literal repetition, wholesale transposition, or rewritings that preserve the core melody? Compare their entrances and give their shared high-register framework.
Compare the notes and rests in the first two bars of the first verse. How are the durations distributed, and how does the attack density change?
In the first complete bar of the bridge, which pitch is initially sustained from the preceding section, and to which pitch does the melody then rise? How long does each last within the bar?

Give the bridge's chord framework and scale degrees. Where does its strongest opening tension chord actually lead, what kind of resolution is this, and how does the progression subsequently return to the minor tonic?
Do the openings of the two verses reuse the same melodic motive? Describe it through the motion of its core pitches.

In which sections do the lead vocal's lowest and highest notes occur? Explain how the spelling of the lowest pitch differs from the key signature, how this relates to the chord's function there, and give the complete range.
In the first bar at the beginning of the second chorus, which pitch is repeatedly emphasized, and which three pitches follow it in sequence?
On which metrical position does the first bar of the first chorus begin singing? How do the consecutive short notes push the final pitch across the barline?

Listen to the first verse and give its complete harmonic framework and Roman-numeral analysis. What type of chord drives the return at the end, which crucial chromatic pitch does it contain, and where does it actually resolve?
After listening to the full track, what broad type of pop sound does it most closely resemble? Name two timbres that most strongly support your judgment.
Across the three choruses, how does the lead melody develop from a basic restatement into an expanded ending? Compare the shared core and the main changes in the first, second, and final choruses.
In the opening, which instrument provides the most prominent harmonic bed? What lighter melodic timbres surround it?

Near the end of the first verse, the harmony suddenly darkens and then pushes toward dominant function. Which chord creates this change, what is its role in the home key, and where does it actually go?

The second chorus largely retains the melody of the first, but two harmonic recolorings are crucial. First identify the home key, then locate both substitutions, state their Roman numerals or functions and actual successors, and explain why the melody remains coherent over them.
As the quiet opening gives way to the first chorus, which newly added rhythmic part most directly changes the sense of momentum? Which accompaniment layers join it to broaden the texture?

Can all three choruses be recognized by the same lead melody? Explain how the final chorus enlarges the climax without changing the core theme, using register, contour, and the added phrase as evidence.
What kind of ascent leads to the melodic high point in the first chorus? After reaching that high note, does the melody continue upward or turn downward?
How do the phrase entrances in the bridge contrast rhythmically with the long notes at its end? Describe the main locations of the rests and how the final few notes are prolonged.

Give a complete account of the first verse's harmonic path: identify the home key, principal chords, and Roman numerals; explain how the added-sixth, ninth, and suspended chords connect; and determine how the ending leads into the chorus.
What is the track's stable metric cycle? Once the drums enter, how do the accents help you identify it?

The opening harmony briefly leaves the tonic center ambiguous. After hearing the entire track, which key should be heard as its ultimate home? Use recurring cadential progressions, one secondary-dominant progression, and the final arrival to explain why the opening color chords do not establish another key.
What are the main rhythmic characteristics of the vocal line in the second verse, and what kind of momentum do they give the section?
Why does the final phrase of the bridge feel more like a pause in anticipation than the preceding phrases? Explain how its note values and final space build energy for the next section.
How does the final chorus expand the earlier, shorter chorus material into the track's concluding climax? Address the melodic register, rhythmic density, and the extension after the vocal ends.
After listening to the whole track, which family of timbres most strongly defines its overall pop sound? Give two examples that recur throughout or stand out in the climaxes.

The three choruses are not simple successive copies. Compare their melodic high points, distribution of rests, and added closing phrases, then summarize how the theme develops across its three appearances.
Why does the rhythm in the first pre-chorus feel progressively more urgent? Determine whether the short-note pattern repeats and explain how rests separate its statements.

Why does the bridge melody sound more speech-like than the preceding chorus rather than continuously spun out? Discuss its register, the gaps between short phrases, and its combination of note values.

The end of the first chorus contains four high-register extension phrases. Give their principal pitches and rhythms, identify the highest pitch and the final sustained pitch, and treat notes tied across barlines as equivalent longer values where appropriate. Adjacent tied eighth notes may also be represented approximately as quarter notes.
After the short introduction, which core section's theme is presented first in full? How does this opening arrangement affect recognition of the theme?
Describe the trajectory of orchestral density from the opening through the choruses, bridge, and outro. What is the most obvious difference between the outro and the earlier full-band textures?
Which sustained background timbre suddenly broadens the space in the bridge, and which acoustic or rhythmic parts combine with it there?
Why does the second chorus feel spacious even though the tempo remains unchanged? Identify the rhythmic relationship among long notes, full-measure rests, and short phrases.

Why is the first verse's harmony more unsettled than an ordinary natural-minor progression? List its analytically significant chromatic chords, give each chord's function or source in the home key and its actual successor, and summarize how they ultimately return to the tonic center.
After listening to the entire track, which sounds most clearly shape its cinematic, spacious pop arrangement? Give two timbral examples from different layers of the texture.
How do the register and melodic direction at the openings of the three choruses differ? Explain how the final entrance returns to the original thematic register afterward.
How is the vocal rhythm in the second verse organized? Identify the most conspicuous relationship between short-note motion and breathing points.

How does the bridge melody gradually build tension from a relatively narrow middle register? Summarize the pitch focus in the first half, the manner of ascent later on, and the direction of the final phrase.

Provide a complete harmonic analysis of the final chorus: identify the home key, specific chords, and Roman numerals; state the opening dominant chord's actual successor; and explain how the ending reconverges on tonic function.
Do the openings of the three choruses sound like three new themes or returns of the same core theme? Give one readily recognizable pitch pattern shared by all three.

From the first verse through the three choruses, how do instrumentation and section length work together to create a gradual expansion? Compare the perceptual roles of the first verse, the first two choruses, and the final chorus.
Why does the vocal line in the second verse feel spacious rather than hurried? Base your judgment on its principal note values and the gaps between phrases.

A raised melodic pitch briefly changes the tonal color in the second chorus. What is the pitch, how does it continue across the chord boundary, and how does the inverted bass in the accompaniment subsequently resolve?

The bridge contains two local harmonic centers. First identify the track's home key, then give the complete principal progression, Roman numerals, and actual destinations of each dominant-function chord, and determine whether this amounts to a global modulation.
After listening to the whole track, what broad type of pop sound does it most closely resemble? Support your answer with two core timbres that persist or recur.

After hearing the full track, what are its most stable tonic center and mode? Cite one actual progression each from the introduction, verse, and bridge or ending, and explain why the other frequently recurring minor chord does not replace the main tonal center.
What are the principal register and type of melodic motion in the first verse? Support your answer with its range and characteristic intervals.
How does the second verse create urgency through short-note bursts that enter late? Describe a typical entrance point, the principal short note values, and the distribution of pauses.

How does the second chorus compress the broad, sustained melody of the first into a tighter version? Reconstruct its principal pitch framework, explain the rhythmic compression, and state whether the ending fully resolves.
After the introduction, in what recurring order do the principal sections unfold? Does the track stop immediately after the third chorus, or is there a separate closing section?

The three verse–chorus cycles are not mechanical copies. Compare the entrances of the three verses and the melodic frameworks of the three choruses, and explain which audible elements are reorganized in the third cycle.
Which three types of parts form the sparse core texture at the opening? Which parts chiefly supply the harmony, and which provides the low-frequency foundation?

Which specific vocal moments in the first chorus best account for its forward-pulling rhythm? Identify at least two pitches and their metric positions or relationships across barlines, then summarize how the section's rhythm is organized.

In the final chorus, a brief chromatic chord is inserted twice into the existing framework. First identify the home key, then name the chord, give its Roman numeral or coloristic source and both actual successors, and determine whether it is passing coloration or the establishment of a new key.
After listening to the full track, which pitch sounds like the ultimate stable center, and is the overall mode major or minor? Cite a recurring dominant–tonic progression as evidence.

How does each of the three choruses enter the tonic-harmony region? Compare the specific chords, Roman numerals, and actual destinations before and after each entrance, and evaluate the relative strength of dominant function in the three cases.
A readily recognizable short melody from the first verse returns later. What is its principal pitch contour, and how is its second appearance changed?
Why does the bridge sound more urgent and continuous than the preceding verses? Compare its phrase-initial space, proportion of short notes, and placement of long notes.
Is the final chorus an exact restatement of the first, or has it been rewritten? Explain the relationship among its opening, the preserved core pitch groups, and the short-note line at the end.
After listening to the full track, what broad kind of pop arrangement does it most closely resemble? Name two core timbres that best support your judgment and explain their roles in the texture.
Trace the principal vocal cycles after the introduction, then explain how the track continues and ultimately closes through instrumental recoloring and an outro after the second chorus ends.
How does the register of the first verse melody change over the course of the section? Use the opening phrase and the high point in the latter half as evidence.
Why does the first chorus melody feel fluid without sounding crowded? Describe how groups of short notes, longer notes, and rests within phrases alternate.

The first verse contains several important chromatic recolorings. Identify the home key and the relevant chords and Roman numerals; explain each chord's source or function and actual successor; and determine the functional region at the end of the verse and how it connects to the chorus.
After listening to the entire track, which pitch is the stable center, and is the overall mode major or minor? Support your answer with a recurring cadential progression.

Why is this track's chorus remembered earlier than in a conventional arrangement where it first appears after a verse? Trace the principal section order after the opening and explain the roles of the third chorus and outro.
What are the main characteristics of melodic motion in the second verse? Identify its recurring registral center and typical kinds of motion.
How does the bridge's rhythmic organization change from its opening to its middle and then its ending? Describe the locations of space, the short-note patterns, and the closing gesture.

Reconstruct the first three phrases of the final chorus's lead melody. Give the main pitches with their quarter- and eighth-note values, and explain how repeated notes in the third phrase prolong its unfinished quality.
What is the stable metric cycle throughout the track? Once the drums enter, which accented positions most clearly support your judgment?

As each of the two pre-choruses enters the chorus, how do melodic register and instrumentation work together to create lift? Compare the end of the pre-chorus, the immediately following chorus entrance, and the changes in the second cycle.
What are the sustained bed and environmental sound at the opening? Which parts provide rhythmic and low-frequency support underneath them?
How does the second pre-chorus create suspense with a “sing–pause–reenter” rhythm? Describe the space in its first two phrases and the contrast between long and short values in the latter half.

The final chorus has a longer harmonic design than the first two. Identify the home key and give the complete principal chords and Roman numerals; explain where each directional chromatic chord actually goes; and describe how the final extended chord closes the color.
After listening to the full track, which group of timbres best characterizes its modern pop arrangement? Distinguish the rhythmic foundation from the melodic and pad layers.

Compare the tonality of the final chorus with the preceding sections. If the tonal center changes, identify the keys before and after, the pivot-point chords and Roman numerals, and use the material that persists afterward as proof.
